summary.text: A 61-year-old woman with severe asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps was referred for progressively worsening eosinophilic otitis media with conductive hearing loss, persistent otorrhea and middle ear granulation. She met 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for EGPA with a cumulative score of 12, was C-ANCA negative and MPO-ANCA positive, and baseline middle ear fluid smear showed eosinophilic predominance.

Initial steroid pulse, prednisolone and cyclophosphamide improved pulmonary and cutaneous manifestations, then intravenous immunoglobulin was given twice for persistent neuropathic symptoms. EOM worsened at age 53 after steroid tapering and responded temporarily to local treatment. Mepolizumab at age 56 gave initial improvement, but EOM and asthma gradually worsened, and prednisolone was raised to 15 mg/day at age 61 without sufficient benefit.

Subcutaneous tezepelumab 100 mg every 4 weeks was started, at a stated age of 60, while she received triple inhaler therapy and theophylline, improving airway symptoms, FeNO and EOM manifestations. After three monthly tezepelumab doses, tezepelumab and mepolizumab were alternated monthly. Otoscopy improved within three months and CT opacities diminished. Left ear air and bone conduction averages were 61.7 and 66.7 dB before alternation, with 41.7 dB air and 51.7 dB bone conduction after 6 months.

Under the alternating regimen prednisolone was tapered from 15 to 5 mg/day over 12 months without recurrence, imaging at 6 months showed sustained resolution of middle ear opacification without further surgery, and repeat smear showed resolution of the inflammatory infiltrate. ACT improved from 18 to 23, MPO-ANCA stayed below 0.2 IU/mL, there was no vasculitic recurrence or adverse event, and the patient reported satisfaction.

ambiguities.issue: Literal source conflict on age: the disease had become refractory at age 61, prednisolone was increased to 15 mg/day without sufficient benefit, and "Given the insufficient clinical response" tezepelumab was started, yet the start is stated at age 60. Both age-bearing sides are quarantined (source_conflict, review_only) on their age/time; the referral age of 61 is not a side because its order relative to tezepelumab is not stated.

evidence.quote: At age 61, her disease had become refractory, and prednisolone had to be increased to 15 mg/day without sufficient benefit
Given the insufficient clinical response, subcutaneous tezepelumab, a human monoclonal antibody targeting TSLP, was initiated at age 60

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not correct either age and do not derive the order of these two events from the ages; the order comes from the "Given the insufficient clinical response" wording only.

ambiguities.issue: The sentence on tezepelumab-related improvement (asthma symptoms, nasal obstruction, FeNO 46 to 19 ppb, EOM) carries citations to a published trial and to an earlier case report by the same author group. Reviewer ruling: the sentence is about this patient ("This upstream TSLP inhibitor" refers back to the tezepelumab started in this patient and the FeNO values are individual measurements); the citations support the general claim. Facts are kept as patient facts.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assume the FeNO values or the specific symptom list come from a cited paper rather than this patient, and do not attach a time to the 46 ppb or 19 ppb values.

ambiguities.issue: Figure 1 pixel content shows peripheral eosinophil values rising to roughly 155/μl at X+3 and about 110-125/μl at several later points after tezepelumab was introduced, while the text says serial peripheral eosinophil counts remained suppressed during the alternating regimen. ambiguities.issue: The abstract describes a bi-monthly alternating regimen, while the body text says tezepelumab and mepolizumab were alternated monthly with each agent given every other month. The two wordings are compatible but not identical.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a different dosing interval for either drug and do not infer the mepolizumab dose during alternation.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Swimlane-style timeline illustrating the clinical course and treatment transitions in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) and eosinophilic otitis media (EOM). The figure displays the temporal relationship between clinical events, oral prednisolone (PSL) dosing, peripheral eosinophil counts, and the administration of biologics (mepolizumab and tezepelumab). The timeline begins with the initiation of biologic therapy and highlights the lack of sustained control with mepolizumab monotherapy, followed by the introduction of tezepelumab and the subsequent alternation of the two agents at four-week intervals. Steroid bursts and clinical relapses are also indicated, providing a visual summary of disease activity and therapeutic response.
